title: Cap. 7 Patrum close: Paschasius, Gregory, Bernard before Scholastics
pass_a_gloss: 8. Paschasius, Library of the Fathers, volume 9, page 930, on those words of Matthew 1:21, He shall save his people from sins, writes thus: Hence Zechariah says, And he has made REDEMPTION OF HIS PEOPLE IN THE HOUSE OF DAVID HIS SERVANT. Therefore the people whom he foreknew as his own he doubtless came to save; all the rest he left by his hidden judgment in the mass of damnation. By which words he teaches that Christ came into the world and underwent death with a certain special intention of saving the predestined — which special intention of effecting the salvation of others he by no means had, however much he willed to make salvation obtainable for all under the condition of Faith. 9. Gregory the Great, Morals, book 22, chapter 18, page 132. For the Only-begotten Son of God to intercede for man is to show himself as man before the coeternal Father; and to have asked for him on behalf of human nature is to have taken up that same nature into the height of his Divinity. He therefore intercedes for us not by voice but by compassion, because what he did not will to be damned in the elect he liberated by taking it up. Those last words especially are to be noted, by which it is clearly indicated that Christ in his whole Mediator's office had a special regard toward infallibly freeing the elect. 10. Bernard on the Psalm He who dwells in the help of the Most High, verse 9. Christ, he says, died for friends — that is, for those to be acquired, namely that he might make friends out of enemies. A little later: So then Christ according to time died for the ungodly, but according to predestination for brothers and friends. Which is as if he had said that Christ dying on the cross had a singular respect toward his predestined brothers and future friends.
pass_b_english: 8. Paschasius (Bibliotheca Patrum, vol. 9, p. 930) on Matthew 1:21, He shall save his people from their sins: Hence Zechariah says, And he made REDEMPTION OF HIS PEOPLE IN THE HOUSE OF DAVID HIS SERVANT. So the people he foreknew as his he surely came to save; all the rest he left, by his hidden judgment, in the mass of damnation. That teaches Christ came and died with a special intention to save the predestined — an intention he did not have for making others' salvation actual, even while he willed to make salvation obtainable for all under the condition of faith. 9. Gregory the Great, Morals 22.18 (p. 132): For the Only-begotten to intercede for man is to present himself as man before the coeternal Father; to ask for human nature is to have taken that nature up into his Divinity's height. So he intercedes for us not by voice but by compassion, because what he would not have damned in the elect he set free by taking it up. Those last words show plainly that in his whole Mediator's work Christ kept a special eye on freeing the elect without fail. 10. Bernard on Psalm He who dwells in the help of the Most High, verse 9: Christ died for friends — that is, for friends to be won, to make friends out of enemies. A little later: So according to time Christ died for the ungodly, but according to predestination for brothers and friends — as much as to say that Christ dying on the cross had a singular regard for his predestined brothers and future friends.
source_text: 8. Paschasius, Biblioth. Patr. tom. 9. pag. 930. in illa verba Matth. i. 21. Saluum faciet populum suum a peccatis, sic scribit, Hinc Zacharias inquit, Et fecit REDEMPTIONEM PLEBIS SUAE IN DOMO DAVID PUERI SUI. Ergo quam sua praescivit, illam proculdubio venit salvare; reliquos omnes occulto suo judicio in massa damnationis reliquit. Quibus verbis docet Christum venisse in mundum, ac mortem subiisse, speciali quadam intentione salvandi praedestinatos, quam specialem intentionem de aliorum salute efficienda minime habuit, utcunque omnibus sub conditione Fidei salutem parabilem reddere voluerit. 9. Gregorius Magnus, moral. lib. 22. cap. 18. pag. 132. Unigenito Dei Filio pro homine interpellare, est apud coaeternum Patrem seipsum hominem demonstrare: eique pro humana natura rogasse, est eandem naturam in Divinitatis suae celsitudine suscepisse. Interpellat igitur pro nobis non voce, sed miseratione, quia quod damnari in electis noluit, suscipiendo liberavit. Notanda sunt imprimis illa ultima verba, quibus clare indicatur, Christum in toto suo officio Mediatorio specialem intuitum habuisse ad electos infallibiliter liberandos. 10. Bernardus in Psalmum, Qui habitat in adjutorio Altissimi, vers. 9. Christus, inquit, pro amicis mortuus est, hoc est acquirendis, videlicet ut amicos faceret ex inimicis. Paulo post, Sic ergo Christus secundum tempus pro impiis mortuus est, secundum praedestinationem autem pro fratribus & amicis. Quod perinde est ac si dixisset, Christum morientem in cruce ad praedestinatos suos fratres & futuros amicos singularem respectum habuisse.
